text: Sorry, I lost you. Can you repeat that, please?
Excuse me, is this seat free?
Yes, please. Two hours, they said. Two hours!
Two hours. Where are you from?
Ireland. A small town near Cork, but I live in Dublin now. And you?
Brazil, São Paulo. Really? Ireland. What do you do there?
I work with horses. And now I am going to Argentina for three months, to work on a farm.
Three months? That is interesting. And then?
Then home, I think. Or maybe not. And what about you? Do you travel a lot for work?
Yes, a lot. I have a company in Brazil. Maybe twenty countries. Who do you travel with?
Alone, always. My sister says I am impossible. She is probably correct, to be fair.

Good evening, ladies and gentlemen. This is an announcement for all passengers on the eight o'clock flight. We are very sorry, but your flight is delayed. The new time is ten fifteen, so that is two hours and fifteen minutes from now. The reason is the weather, not the aircraft. Please stay near the gate, because if the weather changes we can leave earlier, and we will call you. There is coffee and there is water in the room behind you, and it is free tonight for all passengers on this flight. If you have a connection after this flight, please come to the desk now and we will help you. Thank you for your patience.

Hey, it's me. I am still at the airport, two more hours, so I have time to talk. Listen, something funny happened. There is a woman sitting next to me, and normally I say nothing to anybody, you know me. But tonight I asked her one question. Only one: where are you from? And she talked for twenty minutes. Twenty. She is from Ireland, she works with horses, and she is going to Argentina for three months to work on a farm there. I understood maybe half of it, honestly, but she did not care, because I said really and interesting at the right moments and I asked her two more questions. Two hours, and I was not bored, and I did not open the phone once. Anyway. Call me when you land.
